sections.title: Composition / Information on Ingredients
sections.content: Portland Cement (CAS 65997-15-1) 100%. Contains calcium oxide (CAS 1305-78-8), crystalline silica as quartz (CAS 14808-60-7) <1%, and hexavalent chromium compounds (trace). When mixed with water, produces calcium hydroxide (pH 12-14).

sections.title: First-Aid Measures

sections.title: Accidental Release Measures

sections.title: Handling and Storage
sections.content: Avoid dust generation. Use adequate ventilation. Store in dry location. Keep containers closed. Incompatible with acids, aluminum, ammonium salts. Shelf life reduced in humid conditions.

sections.title: Exposure Controls / Personal Protection
sections.content: OSHA PEL: 15 mg/m3 (total dust), 5 mg/m3 (respirable). ACGIH TLV: 1 mg/m3 (respirable, as Portland cement). Crystalline silica PEL: 50 ug/m3. Wear N95/P100 respirator, chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, long sleeves, waterproof boots.

sections.title: Physical and Chemical Properties
sections.content: Appearance: Gray to gray-brown powder. Odor: Odorless. pH: 12-14 (in water). Specific gravity: 3.15. Solubility: Slightly soluble (hydrates). Melting point: >1000°C.

sections.title: Stability and Reactivity
sections.content: Stable under normal conditions. Reacts exothermically with water. Incompatible with acids, aluminum powder, ammonium salts. Produces calcium hydroxide when mixed with water (highly alkaline).

sections.title: Toxicological Information
sections.content: Acute toxicity: Low via oral and dermal routes. Skin: Causes irritation and potential alkali burns with prolonged wet contact. Eyes: Causes serious damage (alkaline pH). Inhalation: Respiratory irritation. Chronic: Crystalline silica component is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen (lung cancer, silicosis).

sections.title: Ecological Information
sections.content: High pH can be harmful to aquatic organisms. Do not allow runoff to enter waterways. Portland cement is not classified as an environmental hazard under GHS.

sections.title: Disposal Considerations
sections.content: Dispose of in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations. Hardened cement can be disposed of as construction debris. Unhardened cement dust should be collected and disposed of as industrial waste.

sections.title: Transport Information

sections.title: First-Aid Measures

sections.title: Fire-Fighting Measures
sections.content: Extremely flammable gas. Flammable range: 2.5%-81% in air. Auto-ignition: 305°C (581°F). Do not extinguish gas fire unless leak can be stopped. Cool cylinders with water spray. Acetylene-air mixtures are detonable.

firstAid.inhalation: Remove to fresh air immediately. If breathing is difficult, give oxygen. If metal fume fever symptoms develop (flu-like symptoms 4-12 hours after exposure), seek medical attention. Chronic overexposure to manganese in welding fume may cause neurological effects.
firstAid.skin: Wash with soap and water. Remove contaminated clothing. For burns from hot metal or slag, cool the burn with water and seek medical attention. Nickel and chromium in fume may cause contact dermatitis in sensitized individuals.
firstAid.eyes: Flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Seek medical attention for flash burns (arc eye/welder's flash). UV radiation from the arc causes photokeratitis.
firstAid.ingestion: Not a likely route of exposure for welding electrodes. If flux coating is ingested, rinse mouth and drink water. Seek medical attention.

ppeRequired: Welding helmet with proper shade lens (minimum Shade 10 for SMAW)
Respiratory protection — NIOSH-approved P100 half-face or powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) for welding fumes
Hearing protection if noise exceeds 85 dBA
fireExtinguishing: Welding electrodes are not highly flammable. Flux coating may be combustible. Use dry chemical, CO2, or water spray. Welding operations are a fire hazard — maintain fire watch per OSHA 1926.352. Keep combustible materials at least 35 feet from welding.
spillProcedure: Pick up dropped electrodes. Sweep up flux coating debris. Avoid generating dust from flux coating. Dispose of electrode stubs properly. No special containment required.
storageHandling: Store in dry location. E7018 low-hydrogen electrodes must be kept in heated rod ovens (120-150°C / 250-300°F) after opening to prevent moisture pickup. Re-dry exposed electrodes at 370°C (700°F) for 1 hour. Maximum exposure time outside oven: 4 hours. Moisture contamination causes porosity and hydrogen cracking in welds.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Product: Excalibur E7018 Welding Electrode. Manufacturer: Lincoln Electric Company, Cleveland, OH 44117. Recommended use: Shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) of carbon and low-alloy steels. Emergency telephone: 1-216-481-8100.

sections.title: Hazard(s) Identification
sections.content: GHS Classification: Specific Target Organ Toxicity (Repeated Exposure) Category 1, Carcinogenicity Category 1A (welding fume), Skin Sensitization Category 1. Signal Word: Danger. Hazard applies to welding fume generated during use.

sections.title: Composition / Information on Ingredients
sections.content: Core wire: Iron (CAS 7439-89-6) ~65%. Flux coating contains: Calcium carbonate, calcium fluoride, iron powder, manganese (CAS 7439-96-5) 1-5%, silicates. Welding fume may contain iron oxide, manganese oxide, fluorides, and trace hexavalent chromium.

sections.title: First-Aid Measures
sections.content: Inhalation: Fresh air; seek medical attention for metal fume fever. Skin: Wash; treat burns. Eyes: Flush 15 min; arc eye requires medical attention. Ingestion: Rinse mouth, drink water.

sections.title: Fire-Fighting Measures
sections.content: Electrode flux is combustible but not highly flammable. Use dry chemical, CO2, or water spray. Maintain fire watch per OSHA 1926.352 during and 30 min after welding.

sections.title: Accidental Release Measures
sections.content: Pick up dropped electrodes. Sweep flux debris. Avoid generating dust. No special containment required.

sections.title: Handling and Storage
sections.content: Store dry. Keep E7018 in heated rod ovens (120-150°C) after opening. Re-dry exposed electrodes at 370°C for 1 hour. Max 4 hours out of oven. Moisture causes hydrogen cracking in welds.

sections.title: Exposure Controls / Personal Protection
sections.content: OSHA PEL for welding fume: 5 mg/m3 (total fume). Manganese PEL: 5 mg/m3 (ceiling). ACGIH TLV for Mn in respirable fume: 0.02 mg/m3. Welding helmet Shade 10+, P100 respirator, FR clothing, leather gloves and boots.

sections.title: Physical and Chemical Properties
sections.content: Appearance: Cylindrical metal rod with gray/brown flux coating. Lengths: 12-18 inches. Diameters: 3/32 to 5/32 inch typical. Melting point of core wire: ~1535°C. Odor: None (fume has metallic odor during welding).

sections.title: Stability and Reactivity
sections.content: Stable under normal storage. Flux coating decomposes during welding, forming shielding gases and slag. Incompatible with strong acids (flux coating may react).

sections.title: Toxicological Information
sections.content: Welding fume is classified as IARC Group 1 carcinogen. Manganese fume: chronic overexposure causes manganism (Parkinson-like neurological disease). Fluorides in fume may cause irritation. Metal fume fever: flu-like symptoms from zinc/copper-contaminated base metals.

sections.title: Ecological Information
sections.content: Welding electrode stubs are recyclable metal. Slag and flux residue should not be discharged to waterways. No significant environmental hazard from unused electrodes.

sections.title: Disposal Considerations
sections.content: Unused electrodes: Recycle as scrap metal. Slag and flux residue: Dispose per local regulations. Welding fume particulate collected by ventilation filters: May be hazardous waste depending on metal content.

sections.title: Transport Information
sections.content: Not regulated as hazardous material for transportation.

sections.title: Regulatory Information
sections.content: OSHA: Hazardous (welding fume). California Prop 65: Welding fume contains chemicals known to cause cancer and reproductive harm (hexavalent chromium, manganese, nickel). SARA 311/312: Acute and chronic health hazard.

sections.content: SDS revision date: 2024-01-20. Always read and follow AWS F1.2 (Laboratory Method for Measuring Fume Generation Rates). Refer to AWS Safety and Health Fact Sheets for additional guidance. ANSI Z49.1 applies to all welding operations.

fireExtinguishing: Non-combustible, but reacts with most metals to generate flammable hydrogen gas. Use water spray, dry chemical, or CO2 for surrounding fire. Do not direct water stream into acid — violent spattering may occur. Contain runoff. Hydrogen chloride gas released on heating.
spillProcedure: Evacuate area. Ventilate. Wear full PPE including acid gas respirator. Contain spill with acid-resistant dike material. firstAid.inhalation: Move to fresh air immediately. If not breathing, give artificial respiration. If breathing is difficult, give oxygen. Seek medical attention. Propane is a simple asphyxiant — high concentrations displace oxygen causing suffocation. Symptoms of oxygen deficiency include rapid breathing, diminished mental alertness, impaired coordination, faulty judgment, and unconsciousness.
firstAid.skin: In case of contact with liquid propane (boiling point -42°C), treat for frostbite. Do not rub affected area. Immerse in or flush with lukewarm water (not hot). Seek medical attention for frostbite.
firstAid.eyes: In case of contact with liquid, flush with lukewarm water for at least 15 minutes. Seek medical attention.
firstAid.ingestion: Not a likely route of exposure. If liquefied gas is ingested, do not induce vomiting. Seek medical attention.

ppeRequired: Insulated gloves when handling liquid propane or cold cylinders
Self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) for emergency response in oxygen-deficient atmospheres
fireExtinguishing: Extremely flammable gas. If safely possible, stop the flow of gas before attempting to extinguish. Use dry chemical or CO2 for small fires. Water spray may be used to cool fire-exposed containers. Do NOT extinguish gas fire unless leak can be stopped — an uncontrolled gas release may lead to explosive reignition. BLEVE (Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapor Explosion) hazard with fire-exposed tanks.
spillProcedure: Evacuate area immediately. Eliminate all ignition sources. Propane is heavier than air and will accumulate in low-lying areas, basements, trenches, and excavations. Ventilate area from a safe distance. Do not enter area without SCBA. Stop leak if safe to do so. Let small releases dissipate.
storageHandling: Store cylinders outdoors or in well-ventilated areas. Keep away from heat and ignition sources. Store upright and secured. Do not store in basements, below grade, or areas without ventilation. Cylinders must comply with DOT requirements. Maximum fill density: 42% for DOT cylinders. Check connections with soap solution for leaks — never use open flame.
